Pearls — particularly the highly prized South Sea pearls — are primarily found in the South Sea (South Pacific Ocean) [d4][d9]. The shells that produce them are located in the southern hemisphere, especially around northern Australia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Burma (Myanmar), and French Polynesia [d4][d9]. The northwest coast of Australia produces most of the world's white South Sea pearls, while the Philippines focuses on the golden variety, and Indonesia also produces large numbers [d3]. Additionally, a rare variety of cultured pearls is found in the Sea of Cortez (Gulf of California) off Guyamas, Mexico [d7]. Beyond saltwater seas, pearls are also produced by freshwater mollusks in rivers and lakes, with China being the world's leading producer of freshwater pearls [d5][d6].
